Hi Sanjay / Priya,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the detailed product walkthrough. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a focused eval: 

Recap from our call:
- Primary workload: user-facing summarization + short Q&A over financial filings (~512 token context, average request 200 tokens).
- Target SLO: p95 generation latency <= 450ms; cost objective: reduce token cost by 30% vs current baseline.
- Quality sensitivity: high for factuality and formatting (tables), moderate for creative wording.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) Shared eval: you send a representative prompt set (we discussed ~200 prompts).
2) Redwood runs a Model Fit & Quantization trade study: baseline FP16 vs GPTQ 4-bit, AWQ 4-bit, and experimental FP8.
3) We provide a short write-up with throughput/latency, per-prompt quality diffs (acceptance criteria: <=2% drop on your core QA metric), and recommended model variant for production.

Next steps / owners:
- Sanjay / Priya: share prompt set + 2 sample documents for context by EOD Wed (5/12).
- Marissa (me): schedule scoped eval and confirm target metrics / acceptance criteria.
- Redwood SE (cc'd): run trade-study and share benchmark link + summary.

Attachments: planning to send an eval plan + quant tradeoffs doc once we confirm prompts.

Marissa / team,

Looping in a few notes from the SE side on models and the tradeoffs we should include in the run: 

Candidate models to test (shortlist):
- Llama2-13B-instruct (good latency/cost baseline for 512-token workloads)
- Mistral-instruct-7B / 7B variants (best cost for lighter workloads, may lose formatting fidelity)
- Falcon-40B-instruct (higher quality on long-context tables but higher baseline cost)
- MosaicML MPT-30B-instruct (strong middle ground)

Quantization paths to compare:
- GPTQ 4-bit (optimized for throughput, medium quality retention)
- AWQ 4-bit (often better quality retention at same bitwidth for Llama-family models)
- FP8 (experimental; can increase throughput on supported HW, may require kernel/path tuning)

Benchmark plan (what I'll run):
- Throughput and p50/p95 latency for cold & warmed KV cache (realistic concurrency: 4-8 qps).
- Per-prompt quality delta using your prompt set: ROUGE / BLEU where applicable + a small set of task-specific metrics you define (factuality checks).
- Token cost estimates (per 1M tokens) for each model/quant combination.

Quick notes on expected tradeoffs based on recent runs:
- AWQ 4-bit typically preserves quality better than generic GPTQ 4-bit on Llama-family models; expect 1-3% relative quality delta vs FP16 on summarization tasks.
- GPTQ 4-bit gives larger throughput gains but sometimes higher degradation on formatting-sensitive prompts.
- FP8 can give throughput similar to 4-bit on some stacks with often lower quality than FP16 but results vary by model.

I'll run the first pass as soon as we have the prompt CSV. Sharing a Drive link to the benchmark folder shortly; I'll attach a short tradeoffs doc and a template eval plan.

—Ethan

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

We ran the initial trade-study against the 200-prompt CSV you provided. High-level summary in-line; full CSV attached (finwave-benchmark-summary.csv) and Drive folder with per-prompt outputs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FinWaveBenchmarks

Key numbers (median across prompts):
- Baseline FP16 (Llama2-13B-instruct): p95 latency = 420ms, throughput baseline = 1x, quality baseline = 100% (reference).
- GPTQ 4-bit (same model): p95 = 180ms (2.3x throughput), observed average quality drop = 2.8% on primary F1 metric; formatting regressions flagged on ~6% of prompts.
- AWQ 4-bit (same model): p95 = 200ms (2.0x throughput), quality drop = 1.1% on primary F1; formatting regressions ~2% (better retention vs GPTQ).
- FP8 (experimental, tuned kernels): p95 = 160ms (2.6x throughput on our test infra), quality drop = 1.9% on primary F1; formatting regressions ~3%.

Interpretation / recommendation:
- If your acceptance threshold is <=2% quality delta, AWQ 4-bit is the safest 4-bit choice for Llama2-13B with a solid throughput win and minimal formatting issues.
- GPTQ 4-bit yields larger perf gains but pushes past the stated acceptance on quality for a non-trivial fraction of prompts (and would require prompt-specific mitigations).
- FP8 shows promise on our infra but is still experimental across our supported stacks — good candidate if you prioritize max throughput and can tolerate a bit more risk.

Next steps:
1) If you want, we can run a focused re-run on the subset of prompts that flagged formatting regressions and test fallback rules (auto-route those prompts to FP16 or AWQ).
2) Run a short human annotation pass on the 30 most critical prompts (we can scope and deliver in 3 business days).
3) If you confirm AWQ 4-bit, we can prepare a recommended config + rollout plan (canary percentages, fallback policy) for production.

Attaching: finwave-benchmark-summary.csv, redwood-quant-tradeoffs.pdf
—Ethan
